text: The white man had known Arsat years before in a distant country, in times of trouble and danger, and he had come to value the young mans courage and loyalty. <break time="0.8s" /> Since then he had often stopped at this house on his journeys, yet he had never heard how Arsat and the woman had come to live hidden in such a place. <break time="0.8s" /> The sun went down, darkness fell swiftly over the lagoon, and the white man, sitting outside by a fire he had made to keep off the mosquitoes, watched the stars appear. <break time="0.8s" /> Far away across the water, the voices of the boatmen died out one by one, and soon the whole world seemed empty and silent under the cold light of the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking of the dying woman, the white man felt in the darkness a strange mixture of fear and fascination, as if the land around him were a battlefield of phantoms. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Arsat came out and sat down by the fire, and after a long silence he asked, Tuan, do you remember my brother, and the white man answered simply, Yes. <break time="0.8s" /> Tuan, I must tell you everything, Arsat began softly, for a man should share his sorrow with a friend, and what the eye has seen is truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Long ago, he said, he and his brother had served as sword bearers to the Ruler of their country, and in those peaceful days he had fallen secretly in love with Diamelen. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a servant of Inchi Midah, the Rulers wife, so that the lovers could meet only in quick glances and in whispers behind the flowering hedges.
